source.title: Revisiting Over-refusal in Safety-aligned Large Language Models: A Representation and Optimization Perspective
source.authors: Chao Chen; Pengyang Shao; Wei Qin; Shi-Jie Hao; Fei Shen; Richang Hong

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares a low-rank subspace derived from harmful-sample gradients with a rank-one mean harmful-gradient direction. It reports that the low-rank subspace performs better, refining the claim toward multiple dominant gradient directions rather than one mean direction.
record.gate_note: The paper does not find or ablate the original harmful-minus-harmless mean-activation direction. It tests gradient subspaces and training-time gradient projection instead. The results included below bear on V4; benchmark results comparing other mitigation methods, layer choices, and GOAL’s overall capability performance are not rows unless they compare the number or identity of gradient directions.
record.test_reason: The paper studies parameter-space gradients of the SFT loss during safety fine-tuning, not the activation-space difference-in-means refusal direction. It never extracts, ablates or adds a harmful-minus-harmless activation direction. Its 'refusal subspace' is the SVD of per-sample LoRA-parameter gradients. Its 'rank-one' comparator is the mean harmful gradient, also in parameter space. So the low-rank versus rank-one result does not bear on V4, which concerns how refusal is represented in activations (affine, cone, or multiple directions). Refusal-direction-style methods (Surgical single-vector ablation, SCANS steering, ACTOR) appear only as baselines, scored on compliance and safety. The paper uses that line of work without testing whether the direction mediates refusal. The gradient findings are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase covers only the Appendix Q side result. The authors' main conclusion is broader. Harmful-sample gradients are highly similar, concentrate in a low-rank subspace, and couple more with refusal-target than helpful-target gradients on over-refusal prompts. Harmful and over-refusal representations are separable at intermediate layers but overlap more in deeper layers. Together these bias over-refusal prompts toward refusal. GOAL (gradient orthogonalization plus contrastive learning) mitigates over-refusal while preserving safety and general capability. They note that gradient coupling is sufficient, not shown to be the sole cause.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines per-sample loss gradients, extracts a low-rank subspace using SVD, and removes its components from over-refusal training gradients. This differs from finding a harmful-minus-harmless mean activation direction and ablating or adding it at model inference.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports gradient-subspace results under different harmful-prompt sources and sample counts, and evaluates projection rank and contrastive-loss weight. The rank-one versus low-rank intervention comparison is reported on Llama-2-7B-Chat.

fits_no_version.finding: On Llama-2-7B-Chat, per-sample SFT gradients for harmful prompts with refusal targets concentrate in a low-rank parameter subspace. CER(10) is 0.78, vs 0.57 for benign+refusal and 0.29 for benign+helpful. The ordering persists after mean-centering (0.59/0.32/0.24).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal supervision on harmful prompts yields low-rank, prompt-dependent parameter gradients beyond a single shared mean-gradient direction.

fits_no_version.finding: Projecting over-refusal gradients against the top-10 harmful-gradient subspace beats projecting against the single mean harmful gradient on all five over-refusal benchmarks. The gain is modest: average C.R. rises from 0.8616 to 0.8738. Random and benign rank-matched subspaces underperform SFT.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For training-time over-refusal mitigation, a multi-direction harmful-gradient subspace is a better projection target than a rank-one mean gradient or non-harmful subspaces.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear-probe separability of harmful vs over-refusal last-token activations peaks at layer 13 (AUC 0.858) and declines to 0.678 by layer 29 in Llama-2-7B-Chat (Table 15).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Distinctions between harmful and superficially-harmful prompts are most linearly available at intermediate layers and erode in deeper layers.

record.problems: The evidence concerns training-time parameter gradients rather than activation-space refusal directions. The direct rank-one versus low-rank comparison is on one model, and the paper gives no uncertainty estimates for the Table 12 or Table 16 benchmark comparisons. The authors also state that their first-order analysis is sufficient rather than proof that harmful-gradient coupling is the sole cause of over-refusal.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows for general capability, safety, overall GOAL benchmark performance, other mitigation methods, or layer selection: those results do not compare or measure the number or identity of refusal-gradient directions. Table 12 PCGrad values are also omitted because they are a generic gradient-surgery comparison, not a direction-count comparison.

untested.parts: No difference-in-means activation direction is extracted, ablated or added.
Jailbreak mechanism and adversarial training against ablation are not studied.
Activation-space affine, cone or multi-direction structure is not tested; only parameter-gradient subspaces are.
Separation of harmfulness judgment from the refusal decision is not tested. Harmful vs over-refusal probe separability is not a harm-vs-refusal dissociation.
No transfer of a refusal direction across languages, variants or base/instruct.
Does not test whether training determines the existence of a single removable direction.

record.verdict_notes: The reader conflated a parameter-gradient 'refusal subspace' with the activation-space refusal direction of V4; all rows are re-linked to none. Rows r7-r36 compare the study's own method variants and controls, so they are method performance rather than claim tests. Surgical (single false-refusal vector ablation), SCANS and ACTOR appear only as Table 1 baselines on compliance and safety, hence uses_without_test/T4. No verdict labels are given.

versions.untested_parts: No difference-in-means activation direction is identified, ablated at every layer and position, or added; the paper does not test whether one such direction mediates refusal while preserving other abilities.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is tested.
The paper does not test whether jailbreaks suppress the claimed activation direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.
The study tests low-rank harmful-gradient structure and compares it with a rank-one mean-gradient direction. It does not test affine or cone descriptions of activation-space refusal directions.
No separate representation of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision is tested.
The study evaluates its own method on multiple model families, but does not test transfer of the claimed difference-in-means direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models.
The study analyzes gradient coupling during safety alignment but does not test how or when refusal training determines whether a single removable direction exists.

rows.subject: Llama-2-7B-Chat
rows.operation_detail: Measured top-10 cumulative explained ratio of per-sample gradients for harmful prompts paired with refusal responses.
rows.uncertainty: Results averaged over five runs; no error bar stated.
rows.note: The paper interprets a higher CER as stronger concentration of gradient energy in fewer directions.
rows.check: Parameter-gradient spectrum (CER of per-sample SFT gradients), not an activation-space refusal direction; a related but different construct.

rows.subject: Llama-2-7B-Chat
rows.operation_detail: Measured top-10 cumulative explained ratio of per-sample gradients for benign prompts paired with the same refusal-response pool.
rows.uncertainty: Results averaged over five runs; no error bar stated.
rows.note: This control shares refusal targets with Harmful+Refusal but has lower gradient concentration.
rows.check: Gradient-spectrum control; does not measure activation-space refusal directions.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Llama-2-7B-Chat gradient-spectrum controls and low-rank-versus-rank-one comparisons
reader_labels.reason: Harmful+Refusal gradients have higher CER(10) than both benign controls, including after centering (r1–r6); Ortho only exceeds rank-one Harmful Mean Ortho on all five reported compliance benchmarks (r7–r16).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The harmful-gradient subspace projection outperforms SFT on four of five benchmarks, while random and benign-gradient subspaces underperform SFT across all five (r17–r36); this supports specificity of the harmful-gradient subspace, not a universal benefit from projecting any directions.
